wu: Awards Nomination Relay: Students stand in two lines. The first student in each line runs to the board, writes a superlative about a classmate (e.g., 'Fatima is the kindest'), and runs back. The next student does the same with a different classmate and superlative.
wuAlt: Superlative Bingo: Each student writes 5 superlatives (e.g., 'the tallest', 'the funniest') on a grid. The teacher calls out classmates' names with superlatives; students mark if they match.
Find Someone Who...: Students walk around asking 'Who is the most...?' (e.g., 'Who is the most helpful?') and write names.
pres: Show 3 flashcards: a student helping (kind), a student running (fast), a student laughing (funny). Model sentences: 'Amina is the kindest. Youssef is the fastest. Omar is the funniest.' Ask 'Who is the kindest?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Realia Awards: Bring in a trophy or medal. Hold it up and say 'This is for the best student in class. Who is the best?' Elicit responses with superlatives.
Class Photo Awards: Show a class photo. Point to students and say 'He is the tallest. She is the prettiest.'
prac: Superlative Survey: In pairs, students ask 3 classmates 'Who is the most...?' (e.g., 'Who is the most creative?') and write names. Teacher monitors and corrects errors. Then, groups share their findings.
pracAlt: Superlative Memory Game: Students sit in a circle. Each student adds a superlative about the previous student (e.g., 'You are the tallest. He is the funniest.').
Superlative Chain Drill: Teacher starts with 'I am the oldest.' Each student says a superlative about themselves or the previous student.
ls: Listen to Award Nominations: Teacher reads 5 award nominations (e.g., 'Karim is the most helpful because he always helps with homework.'). Students write down the winner for each award (e.g., 'Karim').
re: Superlative Charades: One student acts out a superlative (e.g., 'the tallest' by standing on tiptoes), others guess and say the full sentence.
prod: Class Awards Ceremony: In groups, students plan 3 awards (e.g., 'The Best Artist', 'The Funniest Joke') with superlatives. Each group presents their awards and winners to the class.
rw: Ramadan Visitor Guide: Students write 6 tips for visitors during Ramadan using superlatives (e.g., 'The most important tip is to respect fasting hours.'). They use a word bank with 'the most', 'the best', 'the most important'.
st: Song: 'The Best Day Ever' (Super Simple Songs). Students sing along and do actions. Close with 'Today we learned superlatives for class awards. Thank you, class!'
g: Students rotate in pairs, asking 'Who is the most...?' and writing answers.
Students draw a superlative (e.g., 'the fastest') and others guess.
Two teams race to write superlatives about the teacher on the board.
Groups add one sentence with a superlative to a story about Ramadan.
Students throw a ball and say a superlative about the person who catches it.
diff: Fast finishers: Design a trophy for their award winner with a superlative caption.
Support learners: Use a sentence frame '______ is the most ______ because ______.'
hw: Write 3 superlative sentences about your family.
Interview a family member about Ramadan and write 2 tips with superlatives.
Draw a picture of your 'Best Ramadan Day' and write a superlative sentence.
tip: Use peer nominations to build rapport—teens respond well to positive recognition from classmates. Connect superlatives to Ramadan to make language relevant to local culture.
